items.title: Abe Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: we were the opposite band... Coleman Hawkins was the big star. And that was our introduction to the jazz of 52nd Street.

ctx.x: Tell me about Kelly’s Stable in New York.

Yes. That’s the first big thing we ever did. And Kelly’s Stable was that quartet I told you about. It was Pete Sacaponti, a jazz accordion player, Sid — I don’t know if it was Sid Jacobs on bass, and I can’t remember the guitarist. A very nice guitar player. It escapes me. But that was a quartet we had opposite Coleman Hawkins when he made his triumphant return, and this is after – I think after “Body and Soul.” He came to New York from wherever, in Europe, and we were the opposite band.
